title: Delhi Police Departmental Enquiry Appeal: Deadline and Authority
description: A Delhi Police punishment appeal must be filed within 30 days of receiving the order, through your DCP, to the authority set out in DP (P&A) Rule 23(6).
applies_to: Delhi Police officers of subordinate rank (Constable to Inspector) governed by the Delhi Police (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 1980.
answer: Under Rule 24(3) of the Delhi Police (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 1980, file your appeal within 30 days of receiving the punishment order, excluding time taken to get record copies. Submit it through your DCP. Orders of a DCP or ACP go to the Additional Commissioner, and the Additional Commissioner's orders go to the Commissioner.

sections.heading: Which Orders You Can Appeal
sections.body_md:
Appeals lie against orders of dismissal, removal, reduction in rank or pay, forfeiture of service, fine up to one month's pay, withholding of increment and censure [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(1), PDF p. 27)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=27). There is only one appeal from the original order, and the appellate order is final [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(2), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28).

You get a free copy of the appealable order [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(3), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28). You may apply to the disciplinary authority for a copy of the record to prepare your appeal. Preliminary enquiry records are not given unless they also form part of the departmental proceedings [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(4), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28).

sections.heading: Who Hears Your Appeal
sections.body_md:
Rule 23(6) sets the appellate authority according to who passed the original punishment order [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(6), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28):

| Original order passed by | Appellate authority |
|---|---|
| DCP, Addl. DCP, Principal of a Police Training School or College, ACP, or an officer of equivalent rank | Additional Commissioner of Police |
| Additional Commissioner of Police | Commissioner of Police |
| Commissioner of Police | Administrator, Delhi |

sections.heading: The 30-Day Deadline and How to File
sections.body_md:
Send your appeal through the DCP of the district or unit where you serve or served [(DP (P&A) Rule 24(1), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28). It must set out your grounds and enclose a copy of the disciplinary authority's order [(DP (P&A) Rule 24(2), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28).

An appeal not filed within 30 days of receiving the original order, excluding the time taken to obtain the record copy, is barred by limitation. The appellate authority may accept a late appeal if the delay was due to circumstances beyond your control. If you are believed to be evading receipt, the one month runs from the date the order was sent by registered post AD [(DP (P&A) Rule 24(3), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28).

The Delhi High Court upheld the dismissal of an appeal filed about 11 months late, holding that a bare claim of family problems was not sufficient reason for condoning delay [(Ram Sahai Meena v. Commissioner of Police, Delhi HC, 18.03.2010, PDF p. 4)](https://indian-high-court-judgments.s3.amazonaws.com/data/pdf/year=2010/court=7_26/bench=dhcdb/DLHC011644082009_1_2010-03-18.pdf#page=4).

sections.heading: What the Appellate Authority Can Do, and Revision
sections.body_md:
The appellate authority may confirm the order, accept the appeal and set aside the punishment, reduce it, remit the case for further inquiry, or pass other orders [(DP (P&A) Rule 25(1), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28) [(DP (P&A) Rule 25(1), PDF p. 29)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=29). It may enhance the punishment only after a fresh show cause notice and a reasonable opportunity, including a personal hearing if asked for [(DP (P&A) Rule 25(1)(d), PDF p. 29)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=29). Every appellate order must give reasons, and you get a free copy [(DP (P&A) Rule 25(2), PDF p. 29)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=29).

If your appeal is rejected, you cannot file a second appeal. You may file a revision within a month of receiving the appellate order, to the authority above the appellate authority, on grounds of material irregularity or illegality [(DP (P&A) Rule 25-A, PDF p. 29)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=29).

sections.heading: Where to Check
sections.body_md:
- Rules 23 to 25-A of the Delhi Police (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 1980, in the India Code booklet [(DP (P&A) Rules 23-25, PDF p. 27)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=27).
- The date stamp or receipt on your copy of the punishment order, because the 30 days run from receipt.
- Civilian staff in Delhi Police are governed by the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 or their parent department's rules, not these rules [(DP (P&A) Rule 3(ii), PDF p. 17)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=17).

faqs.q: What is the time limit for a Delhi Police departmental appeal?
faqs.a: 30 days from receipt of the original order, excluding time taken to obtain the record copy [(DP (P&A) Rule 24(3), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28).

faqs.q: Can a late appeal be accepted?
faqs.a: Yes, if the appellate authority finds the delay occurred due to circumstances beyond your control [(DP (P&A) Rule 24(3), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28). A vague reason may not be enough [(Ram Sahai Meena, Delhi HC, 18.03.2010, PDF p. 4)](https://indian-high-court-judgments.s3.amazonaws.com/data/pdf/year=2010/court=7_26/bench=dhcdb/DLHC011644082009_1_2010-03-18.pdf#page=4).

No. There is only one appeal [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(2), PDF p. 28)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=28), but a revision can be filed within a month of the appellate order [(DP (P&A) Rule 25-A, PDF p. 29)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=29).

Yes. Censure is one of the orders against which an appeal lies [(DP (P&A) Rule 23(1), PDF p. 27)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=27).
